title: Car v pedestrian at 15th and Exchange Saturday - The Daily Astorian
content: On Saturday at around 10 a.m., a person was hit in a car vs. pedestrian accident near 15th and Exchange. The driver, Elsa Nethercot was charged with careless driving, a class B traffic violation. Although one pedestrian was involved and went to Columbia Memorial Hospital after the incident, there were no injuries reported. According to Astoria Police Chief Stacy Kelly, Nethercot was driving south on 15th Street and turned left on Exchange when she said was blinded by the morning sun. Two pedestrians were in the crosswalk — one was able to jump out of the way of the oncoming vehicle while the other person was hit by the car. While no injuries were reported, said Kelly, the person went to Columbia Memorial Hospital, though it was unclear if they were transported there or went by themselves. Kelly said all traffic incidents like this are reported to ODOT and the city’s traffic engineering department and are also reviewed by the Traffic Safety Advisory Committee which meets quarterly. The next time the committee will meet is on Oct. 27. Thank you for reading the The Astorian.Subscribe to get Unlimited Access to our website.

title: Tory Burch x Dimepiece at 7 Spring - V Magazine
content: On October 7th, Brynn Wallner of Dimepiece hosted an evening at 7 Spring, the members’ club in Manhattan. Editors, designers, stylists, tastemakers, and more gathered for backgammon and cocktails to celebrate the new Eleanor Curve watch collection by the luxury fashion and accessories house. Remi Davenport, a backgammon instructor, taught attendees and led games on custom boards. The watches, of course, were also customizable on-site. With a vintage feel but modern flair, the Eleanor Curve can be worn by everyone. Notable guests included Ella Emhoff, Samira Ahmed, Natalia Spotts, Marlien Rentmeester, Aminatou Sow, Emily Dawn Long, Chrissy Rutherford, and many more. Brynn Wallner founded Dimepiece as an effort to celebrate women and watches—what better event for her to host than the launch of Tory Burch’s newest timepiece? Blinkink has revealed that one of its accomplished creators, London-based director and animator Renee Zhan, directs a new segment for Shudder’s latest instalment of the horror anthology franchise V/H/S/Mixtape. Titled Dance, Dance, Dance, Dance, the piece features original puppets from Jim Henson’s Creature Shop. The ninth film in the V/H/S franchise, V/H/S/Mixtape is produced by Be Afraid Media, Bloody Disgusting, Cinepocalypse Productions, Image Nation Films, Shudder, Speed Demon and Spooky Pictures. Taking the franchise in a new musical direction, it explores the darker side of music, sound and rhythm through a collection of new horror stories. Zhan’s Dance, Dance, Dance, Dance is set in a studio attempting to reboot a long-cancelled puppet show with a mysterious past, turning the familiar world of children’s television into something considerably more unsettling. “Puppets, musicals and horror are all the things I love, so it was a dream to combine the three into one mad film,” Zhan shared. “And even more so to work inside the legendary Jim Henson Creature Shop and bring some puppets to life with the best in the world.” Zhan’s work spans stop-motion, 2D animation, puppetry and live-action filmmaking, and has screened at prestige international festivals such as Sundance, TIFF, SXSW and Annecy. Her 2019 film Reneepoptosis won the Sundance Jury Prize for Animated Short. Watch V/H/S/Mixtape on Shudder and see more of Renee Zhan’s work at blinkink.co.uk. title: Curious About the Future of the Alfa Romeo Giulia? This Beautiful Concept Could Be a Clue - Car and Driver
content:
The concept houses a hybrid version of Alfa’s twin-turbo V-6 and blends the styling of a grand tourer with that of a supercar. Alfa Romeo may not lead the sales charts, and the products it builds may not always be the most reliable, but the Italian marque will be damned if you don’t gaze upon its sheetmetal with a “****, that car looks incredible.” Your mileage may vary, but our introduction to the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso, the newest concept car from the Italian marque, was met with a string of words that have long been deemed unsuitable for FCC airwaves. According to the automaker, the new concept is a hair longer and wider than a Giulia Quadrifoglio. That size appears to be intentional, with Alfa describing the proportions as a blend between the character of a grand touring car and the character of a supercar. The result is an exceedingly shapely design, a 2+2 configuration complete with coach doors, and a reported curb weight of just 3858 pounds. See all results for used Alfa Romeo for sale near 85032 We say “just” in regard to a nearly two-ton vehicle because Alfa confirmed that the concept is powered by a hybridized version of the brand’s twin-turbocharged 2.9-liter V-6. Unfortunately, the automaker didn’t reveal any other specs for the car, so power figures will have to wait until an actual production derivative is built. The brand did share a few details, though, including that the Cuorerosso features air suspension, as well as a steer-by-wire system. The exterior is littered with Alfa Romeo’s design cues. The grille takes on the familiar Scudetto shape and features the equally familiar cross and Biscione graphics borrowed from the Alfa Romeo logo. The wheels are a new take on the classic “telephone” wheel design, while Alfa’s Quadrifoglio logo sits behind the front fenders. While there are a number of elements on the exterior that we could see making it into a production car, Alfa leaned much more heavily into the concept of it all for the interior. The dashboard is bare, save for the essentials. There are two gauges, two air vents, a futuristic-looking shifter, and a handful of physical controls in the center stack that Alfa is calling the “Magma Display.” Unfortunately, the automaker doesn’t seem to have any plans to put the Cuorerosso into production. Alfa confirmed that the concept is not “an anticipation of a production model” but instead serves as a “manifesto destined to inspire future models,” as well as a preview for how the brand plans to electrify its lineup. Next-generation 24 kW power delivery board converts 800 VDC directly to 12 VDC in a single stage, eliminating the 50 V IBC power stage, boosting system efficiency and reducing board space. The solution will be showcased in the NVIDIA AI Factory MGX Ecosystem partner display area at OCP Navitas Collaborates with NVIDIA on 800 V-to-12 V Power Delivery Board for Next-Generation AI Infrastructure TORRANCE, Calif., Oct. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Navitas Semiconductor (Nasdaq: NVTS), a leader in next-generation power semiconductors and power delivery solutions, pioneering GaN, high-voltage and ultra-high-voltage SiC, and IVR technologies, today announced its latest 24 kW, 800 V-to-12 V DC-DC power delivery board (PDB), powered by GaNFast™ technology and developed in collaboration with NVIDIA, to support the NVIDIA MGX ecosystem and advance 800 VDC power architectures for AI data centers. The new PDB is planned to be featured on NVIDIA's AI Factory MGX Wall partner display area at OCP Global Summit 2026. This latest 24 kW, 800 V-to-12 V PDB extends Navitas' portfolio of 800 VDC AI data-center platforms, building on the previously announced 20 kW, 800 V-to-6 V PDB developed in collaboration with NVIDIA. These solutions advance the core strategic focus of the Navitas 2.0 transformation to accelerate the replacement of legacy silicon with next-generation GaN and SiC high-power technologies across AI infrastructure, from Grid-to-xPU. The PDB is capable of delivering 24 kW with a target efficiency of 97% at full load and a power density exceeding 2,000 W/in³, providing power for the entire compute tray. Designed in NVIDIA's latest 400 mm × 60 mm form factor, the PDB can be integrated onto the compute motherboard as close as possible to the xPUs, minimizing power-delivery losses and supporting high-power demands. The single-stage architecture converts 800 VDC directly to 12 VDC, eliminating the existing 50 V-to-12 V IBC conversion stage and delivering 12 V directly to the voltage regulator module (VRM) that powers the xPU. This simplified power architecture improves system efficiency and reliability while reducing power losses, board space and overall power-delivery complexity. The power architecture incorporates 16 × NV6034 (650 V, 18 mΩ) GaNFast™ FETs on the primary side, configured in a stacked half-bridge topology and featuring Navitas' latest dual-cooled DFN 8 × 8 package. "The next era of AI will be defined not only by how much compute we can create but by our ability to deliver the power needed to unleash its full potential," said Chris Allexandre, President and CEO of Navitas. "Our collaboration with NVIDIA is breaking the AI infrastructure power wall by reimagining power delivery from 800 VDC to the GPU. This next-generation 24 kW solution demonstrates how GaNFast™ technology can eliminate power-conversion stages, increase efficiency and power density, and bring power closer to the GPU." Navitas' portfolio of 800 VDC AI data-center platforms provides customers with greater flexibility to select the optimal intermediate-bus voltage and VRM architecture for their point-of-load power requirements. The 800 V-to-12 V PDB is planned to be showcased at the NVIDIA AI Factory MGX Wall partner display area at OCP Global Summit 2026. For more information, please contact your Navitas representative or email info@navitassemi.com. About NavitasNavitas Semiconductor (Nasdaq: NVTS) is a leader in next-generation power semiconductors and power delivery solutions, pioneering GaN, high-voltage and ultra-high-voltage SiC, and IVR technologies for AI infrastructure, including data centers and energy and grid systems, as well as additional markets such as high-performance computing and industrial electrification. Collectively, these technologies address the complete grid-to-xPU power architecture, breaking the AI infrastructure power wall and enabling higher efficiency, greater power density, and increased performance across the entire power chain. Navitas' GaNFast™ FETs deliver industry-leading power density, efficiency, and high-speed performance, while GaNFast™ power ICs integrate GaN power, drive, control, sensing, and protection to enable faster, more efficient power conversion, leading to smaller and more reliable systems. The GeneSiC™ portfolio combines proprietary trench-assisted planar (TAP) SiC technology with leading-edge discrete packaging and SiCPAK™ power modules to deliver industry-leading efficiency, ruggedness and performance. Claros™ IVR technologies extend power delivery directly to the xPU, enabling customers to implement vertical power delivery (VPD) and embedded power delivery (EPD) architectures with high-density power conversion beneath or within millimeters of the processor, minimizing power-delivery losses and impedance while enabling ultra-fast transient response, higher efficiency and maximum power density. title: Obituary information for Richard V. Massey - Solimine Funeral Home
content: Richard Vincent Massey, age 88 of Swampscott, MA and Oldsmar, Fl, passed away peacefully on Tuesday, October 6, 2026.  Born in Swampscott, MA, he was the son of the late John and Gertrude (Carpenter) Massey.  Dick was the devoted husband of the late Johanne (Andersen) Massey with whom he shared 44 years of marriage. He was a lifelong resident of Swampscott, graduating from Swampscott High School with the class of 1956.  Growing up on the hill with his many friends, he was an exceptional athlete, greatly enjoying the camaraderie of his friends and teammates.  Following his high school graduation, Dick took his talents to Saint Lawrence University where he was a key player on the 1961 National Championship runner-up hockey team.  After college, the now married Dick and Johanne came home to Swampscott where he began work at Massey Plumbing & Heating Co., which today is recognized as the oldest continuously operating business in Swampscott.  During his post college time, Dick played in the New England Hockey League and refereed High School Hockey with his family in tow for many memorable moments.  As the first coach for Swampscott Youth Hockey, he was instrumental in the program’s inception.  Dick was recognized for his athletic achievements and contributions with his election to The Swampscott High School Athletic Hall of Fame. From summers in Ossipee, NH, spring trips to Oldsmar, FLA, winters skiing at Sugarloaf, ME, golfing around the North Shore and membership at Tedesco Country Club and Fox Hollow, The Massey Family could not have had a better upbringing.  In retirement, Dick enjoyed his time between Swampscott, MA and Oldsmar, FL, living his life well lived. His legacy is carried on through his four-(4) sons and their families; Rick and Ann Massey of Swampscott, MA; Michael and Cara Massey of Swampscott, MA; Peter and Kelly Massey of Lynn, MA; and, Jeff Massey of Swampscott, MA; six-(6) grandchildren; Brendan and Julia Massey; Justin Massey and his wife Hypatia and Trevor Massey; Alyson Massey; and Adeline Massey; and his three-(3) great-grandchildren; Ezme and Chase Massey; and Aria Massey. For the past decade he found comfort in the loving companionship of Claire Kirk and her family; Deborah Kirk of Swampscott, MA; Mike and Shawna Kirk and family of Beverly, MA; Kevin and Kim Kirk and family of Matthews, NC. Dick was a proud brother to his sister Donna Massey of Natick, MA; the late John “Jack” Massey who is survived by his wife Jif of San Clemente, CA; and the late Anne (Massey) Burnham who is survived by her husband Charlie of Stafford, NH. He was the son-in-law of the late Ty and Eleanor Andersen of Swampscott; brother-in-law to Ty and Deborah Andersen of Lakeland Fla; and to the late Dean Andersen of Swampscott, MA. 'What I was trying to understand was, what does it actually mean to make light,' says Gabriel Hendifar, artistic director of Apparatus. The question led him to Act V: Afsaneh, the New York design studio’s first new collection in five years, and a meditation on creativity, knowledge and the cycles of life. 'I really needed a moment to understand what I was saying and why,' he says of the time between collections. Hendifar had created an impressive body of work over the past 14 years, and wanted to consider 'the kinds of things and the ways of making that feel relevant now.' In previous Acts, he channeled the glamour of late-1970s New York, the 'sparkly creative expression' of the Wiener Werkstätte, a reimagining of his family’s Iranian history and a playful vision of the future. With Act V, 'I am trying to make sense of where we are collectively by looking back at the cycle of the seed and the flower, and what it can mean for us to hold ideas dear and to amplify them.' Afsaneh, which is both his mother’s name and the Persian word for fable, unfolds in four series: Esfand, the seed, symbolizing the mother; Gol, the flower, the amplification of the seed; Rahvi, the serpent and collector of knowledge; and Jahaan, the cosmos, where the seed, flower and knowledge are shared. As for materials, Hendifar explains, 'We’re working with materials that say something about the future, and something about the past, and place the work in an atemporal place.' The seed becomes the collection’s building block, appearing in sconces, vessels and an incense burner. 'They feel like their own little universe, like they hold the entirety of the cosmos,' Hendifar says. In Gol, cast-glass seeds are enveloped by large fiberglass shades that suggest (depending on one’s point of view) flower petals, jellyfish or octopuses. 'This is the seed wrapped in beauty as a way to both protect it and attract the people who are meant to seek it,' he adds. The amulets in Rahvi are crafted from seven semi-precious stones, including tiger’s eye, lapis lazuli and red jasper. Like the flower, they embody both amplification and protection. 'This is almost like a spiritual starter kit for leaning into the light,' he jokes. The final series, Jahaan, centers on the table. 'It’s where we gather to share knowledge. It’s where we gather to share food. The table is the idea of community.' As with previous Acts, Afsaneh incorporates scent and performance. The fragrance, with notes of damask rose and oud, evokes what Hendifar calls 'moonlight in a desert rose garden.' This year he debuted five short films, made in collaboration with the Martha Graham Dance Company. Hendifar, who grew up as a musician and self-described theatre kid, sees film as another block in building each Act. 'It allows me to say a lot of things in a way that isn’t always so direct…it can feel like a collage.' When scheming a new collection, he asks, 'What are we telling people in movement, sound and music? And what is the moment when we are gathering in a room together? What does it feel like to be at the party?' For Hendifar, it’s about creating a world people want to enter, and leaving them with something that lingers long after they leave. Generally speaking, the CAA’s Title V Operating Permit program is a vehicle to compile and assure compliance with “applicable requirements” that other CAA programs impose on the source; it is not an opportunity to substantively reconsider the requirements themselves. That distinction is important because Title V has unique federal oversight tools that can disrupt permitting, including mechanisms for EPA to object to the issuance of a facility’s state-issued Title V operating permit and cause the permit to be modified, revoked, or terminated. Title V also establishes a related process for members of the public to petition EPA for such an objection, with exceptionally tight deadlines that can quickly force an EPA response. EPA’s final rule codifies an approach the agency had developed in a pair of Title V orders, Hunter and Big River Steel, both issued in October 2017. Under that approach, when an NSR permit is issued subject to requirements for public notice, opportunity for public comment, and opportunity for judicial review, the resulting terms and conditions are the NSR-related “applicable requirements” under Title V and cannot be revisited during the Title V permitting process. That principle extends to NSR permit content, such as Best Available Control Technology (BACT) determinations, and whether major or minor NSR applies. Limited Title V review remains available where NSR requirements have not been conclusively established, including where no NSR permit was issued, or the requisite opportunities for public participation and judicial review were not available. Separately, but also notably, the final rule also clarifies that the General Duty Clause of CAA Section 112(r)(1) is not an “applicable requirement” according to EPA’s statutory interpretation of Title V. However, accident-prevention requirements under CAA Section 112(r)(7) remain subject to Title V’s definition of “applicable requirements.” The Title V final rule on “applicable requirements” is the latest in a series of recent developments related to NSR. The changes and proposed changes are particularly relevant to companies planning to develop data centers, onsite generation, or to undertake other major capital projects, where air permitting requirements can often affect construction schedules. EPA guidance and rulemakings, federal court decisions, pending legislation, and enforcement litigation are addressing when NSR applies, how sources calculate emissions, when construction may begin, and how NSR disputes should be resolved: NSR developments are not limited to EPA. In Congress, several pieces of proposed legislation would alter aspects of NSR permitting. For example, the House Energy and Commerce Committee has reported out: In the courts, NSR enforcement litigation remains consequential. Earlier this year in United States v. EES Coke Battery, LLC, the Eastern District of Michigan imposed a $100 million civil penalty and injunctive relief for NSR violations, and held not just the plant owner liable, but also several other affiliated entities liable as “operators” due to the high degree of control they exhibited over the facility. United States v. EES Coke Battery, LLC, 820 F. Supp. 3d 600 (E.D. Mich. 2026). Given the stakes for project timing and the highly fluid NSR landscape, companies must consider how these recent and ongoing developments affect applicability analyses, construction sequencing, offset acquisition, compliance documentation, and overall air permitting strategy. And these relatively recent developments capture only part of the broader range of NSR issues that may arise, including source-determination questions such as common control and adjacency, project aggregation and “circumvention,” and the scope of what constitutes a major modification. In the case of EPA’s recent rule clarifying “applicable requirements” under Title V, a principal benefit is that it formally limits opportunities to use the Title V process as a “second bite at the apple” for NSR determinations—some of which, as in Hunter, may be decades old. At the same time, the rule does not eliminate other avenues to challenge or enforce NSR requirements. By expressly limiting the extent to which underlying NSR determinations can later be revisited through Title V, the rule may instead place greater importance on strategic decisions made during the initial preconstruction permitting process, when public participation, agency review, and potential litigation can have immediate consequences for project schedules. Companies planning new facilities or modifications to existing ones should therefore consider not only whether and how NSR applies, but also how best to develop a defensible permitting record at the outset. title: Astrometric Planet Search Around Southern Ultracool Dwarfs: V. Discovery Of The Exoplanet Candidate PALTA-1 b - Astrobiology Web
content:
[astro-ph.EP]    We report the discovery of PALTA-1 b, a sub-Jupiter mass exoplanet candidate orbiting the nearby early-L dwarf DENIS-P J1253108-570924 (DE1253-57) located at a distance of ~17 pc. The exoplanet was discovered by monitoring the L dwarf’s astrometric motion with FORS2 at the Very Large Telescope over more than eight years and characterising the deviations from the expected single-source motion. The estimated planet mass is between 0.54 MJup and 0.77 MJup, depending on the uncertain mass of the ultracool dwarf host. The system’s mass ratio is about 0.010, and the relative separation is estimated at 1.6-3.4 au. If confirmed, PALTA-1 b would be one of the very few known examples of a giant planet orbiting a nearby ultracool dwarf. This discovery finalises a larger astrometric planet search survey that targeted 20 nearby ultracool dwarfs and previously discovered three new ultracool binary systems. J. Sahlmann, P. F. Lazorenko, E. L. Martín, D. Ségransan, M. Mayor, S. Udry Comments: 12 pages, 10 figures. title: Wales v Albania: Rhian Wilkinson wary of Albania with record run in sight - BBC
content: Rhian Wilkinson is under contract as Wales boss until 2029 Rhian Wilkinson insists Wales must take nothing for granted despite a 1-0 advantage going into their World Cup play-off semi-final second leg against Albania on Tuesday. Wales are favourites to move a step closer to a first World Cup after their narrow first-leg success. Wilkinson's side will achieve their longest unbeaten run of 10 games if they come through unscathed from the match in Llanelli. But the Wales head coach believes it would be foolish to think the job is close to being done against Albania after saying her team "got away with one" in Shkoder last Friday. "That Albanian team are right on the edge of something special because they really fight for everything," Wilkinson said. "When I speak to the older, more experienced players with Wales, they remember being that team that is ranked lower but is scrapping and fighting for everything and they get results because they catch people unaware. "We're very aware of them - this is a dangerous Albanian team. We need to make sure we don't sit back and rest because they're going to be knocking on the door." Women's World Cup qualifying play-off semi-final second leg Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC One Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary. Wales thrashed Albania 4-0 when the nations met during the group phase of qualifying in Wrexham in April. But they scraped a 1-0 away success in the return group match and duly repeated the trick courtesy of an unconvincing performance three days ago. Wales are ranked 31st in the world - 37 places above the Albanians - but Wilkinson knows her players must match their opponents' "effort and pride" to triumph at Parc y Scarlets. "It's one where you better expect to be crawling off the field exhausted if you want to be walking away with a successful game." Players should expect to crawl off field - Wilkinson Victory in Albania last week saw Wilkinson's side match the record nine games without defeat set between November 2013 and August 2014. Head coach Wilkinson was unaware of the potential landmark tenth unbeaten game on the eve of Albania's visit. "What a wonderful record [that would be] for me to have, but more than anything, this is about the team showing up for each other and delivering to a standard we can be proud of," she said. "Win or lose, this is a very special team and I'll stand with them all day. But we know we want to be better for ourselves and equally for the fans." Wales are still without nine regular squad members due to injury with the likes of Olivia Clark, Hayley Ladd, Rhiannon Roberts, Ffion Morgan and Ceri Holland - arguably their most influential player since Jess Fishlock's retirement - all missing. Wilkinson hopes a number of the absentees will be fit should they progress to a two-legged play-off final in early December. Wales are likely to face Norway - who won 2-0 in Romania in their semi-final first leg - in the next stage. Even if they were to shock Norway, Wales may then have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a place in Brazil. So Wilkinson is not yet contemplating the idea of reaching a World Cup with so many potential games to go. She said: "It's one step at a time. We don't get ahead of ourselves [because] it's about that peak in the distance that we're working towards." Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week? title: Highly anticipated Fabio Wardley v Daniel Dubois rematch live on BBC Radio 5 Live, with watchalong on BBC iPlayer and YouTube - BBC
content: The pair will meet again in London just months after their dramatic first encounter in May BBC Radio 5 Live and BBC Sounds will bring fans live commentary of one of the most eagerly anticipated heavyweight fights of the year when Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley renew their rivalry on Saturday 17 October. The pair will meet again in London, with the WBO heavyweight title on the line, just months after their dramatic first encounter in May. Dubois survived two early knockdowns before producing a remarkable comeback to stop Wardley in the 11th round, in a fight widely regarded as one of the most dramatic heavyweight contests of 2026. Now the pair go head-to-head again. Two-time world champion Dubois will be looking to prove his first victory was no fluke, while Ipswich's Wardley will be out for revenge and the chance to reclaim his place among the heavyweight division's stars. Listeners can follow every round live on BBC Radio 5 Live, with commentary and expert analysis available across BBC Radio 5 Live and BBC Sounds, alongside coverage across the BBC Sport website and app. Stacey Copeland and Steve Bunce lead the coverage, with former Super-middleweight World Champion Richie Woodhall and Ronald McIntosh providing commentary, and Molly Stephens reporting from ringside. Fans can watch the live stream on the BBC Sport YouTube channel and BBC iPlayer, while getting involved throughout the evening with their own opinions, questions and reactions across BBC Sport's digital and social platforms. Widely regarded as a contender for fight of the year, the May thriller saw Dubois hit the canvas twice before turning the fight on its head and stopping Wardley in the 11th. title: Police officer injured as 10 arrests made at tense Liverpool v Manchester City match - The Guardian
content: Police officer taken to hospital with serious facial injury Five people arrested on suspicion of tragedy chanting A police officer sustained a serious facial injury while making an arrest after the Liverpool v Manchester City match at Anfield on Sunday, Merseyside police have said. The fixture was highly charged as City played their first match since it was confirmed they had been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. Merseyside police said 10 arrests had been made, with one man arrested on suspicion of two offences of assaulting a constable, five on suspicion of tragedy chanting, one on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly and assault, two for affray and one on suspicion of throwing items on the pitch. The police said that during one of those arrests, at 6.35pm on Anfield Road, an officer sustained a serious facial injury. Police said the officer had been taken to hospital and was recovering at home. “The officers and stewards are there to protect the public and keep them safe, and it is extremely disappointing that an officer has sustained a serious injury while carrying out that duty,” Ch Insp Leanne Hobin said. “Inquiries into the full circumstances are ongoing so that anyone responsible for criminality can be brought to justice.” On the arrests for tragedy chanting, Hobin said: “The tragic loss of life should never be a subject for tribal point scoring. Football fans who chant about tragedies cause huge distress to the loved ones of people who died and their behaviour has absolutely no place in football. We will continue to work with clubs to take action to identify any perpetrators and bring them to justice.” She said the “overwhelming majority” of spectators behaved well. City won the match 3-0.

title: The Modern V-Twin That Could Become A Future Classic - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update It's hard to predict what's going to become the next sought-after motorcycle. But there are some earlier indicators that can help identify the next true classic. Was the model popular in its day? Maybe it was underappreciated? Was it expensive? Another indicator could be the use of rare components. Or perhaps there was a collaboration between two manufacturers, like it was with the Harley-Davidson's partnership with Porsche on the polarizing V-Rod. Whatever the reason, owning a bike that is the envy of all riders is truly special. There have been many bikes, in the last 100+ years of motorcycle culture, that have remained in our hearts and minds. We're talking about one of the latest examples of that, and it comes from Harley-Davidson. One of the biggest hints that a bike is a future classic is whether it was based on a popular racing bike of the time. And there have been many such bikes over the years. Right now it may not look like it, but the recently dumped Indian FTR, based on the prestigious FTR750 flat track bike, may turn into a classic someday. Or the Indian Challenger RR with its race-spec componentry. Another recent racing replica was Triumph's Daytona Moto2 765, featuring the motor from its MotoGP Moto2 collaboration. It had some fantastic features and equipment, and was limited to only 1,530 production bikes (765 for Europe and 765 for U.S. markets). Several other examples come to mind from brands like Ducati, BMW, Kawasaki, and even KTM. Things take a turn when you actually laser in on modern V-twin race-replica machines. Indian's Challenger RR is a prime example, and so is the Aston Martin AMB 001. But other than that, the list is slim. What about Harley-Davidson, you ask? Well, you could say Harley-Davidson has a complicated relationship with racing. It has dipped its toe into it on multiple occasions, starting with its board track racing, Flat Track Racing, and even an honest-to-goodness superbike, the VR1000. And yes, the VR1000 is rare and expensive, with one model selling for $104k. All of these are from years ago, though, which makes finding a 'modern V-twin' that could become a future classic quite difficult. It's not impossible, however, and the recent CVO Road Glide RR serves as the answer. Taking full advantage of the King of the Baggers popularity, Harley built the RR on the bones of its factory racing bikes. Knowing full well that it would be an expensive model from the start, and that nobody in their right mind would ever race it for real, Harley crammed it full of tech goodies, performance mods, and faux racing details to make even the biggest Ducati Panigale V4 fans drool with jealousy. Chief among these was the Screamin' Eagle 135ci engine—Harley's biggest, baddest, and most powerful engine on a production bike to date. This exceptional, and expensive, piece of machinery had an aggressively limited run of only 131 production models. So it's no wonder that its original price has only gone up even more on the secondary market. You thought $110k was too much? Well, buckle up, buttercup, because one just sold for $152k in the used market. That's supercar territory. You could get a used Aston Martin Vantage for that kind of cash. And those are a lot more practical, believe it or not. So what exactly differentiates the RR from a standard Road Glide that only costs $26k? Let's run the list. The exhausts were made from titanium. The bodywork is entirely made of carbon fiber. And there are custom billet aluminum components throughout the bike. But that's not what makes it special. For anyone complaining that Harley only makes heavy, slow bikes, the American bike maker tuned its Screamin' Eagle V-twin to produce 153 horsepower and 150 ft-lb of torque. Coupled with its Screamin' Eagle internals, Racing King 6 Transmission, High Performance Intake System, and feather-light exhaust (courtesy of Akrapovič), the RR is Harley's most powerful bagger to date. It's unlikely we'll see a Harley with such a serious engine again (thanks to its new approach on value), which is precisely why this modern V-twin can go on to become a future classic. To make all that racing horsepower and torque work on the street, Harley continued the premium component build-out with the rest of the features on the RR. To help with aggressive lean angles and cornering on your favorite twisty roads, race-spec Öhlins were installed to raise the ride height by two inches. For reference, the front suspension has Öhlins 43mm FGR inverted forks, while the rear comprises dual Screamin' Eagle Öhlins Remote Reservoir shocks. Topping things off, the swingarm is made of billet aluminum and weighs just 18 lbs. Bringing this beast to a halt are GP4-RX Brembos that deliver MotoGP-level braking power. Cast aluminum wheels, billet aluminum mid-foot controls, and a Saddlemen solo racing seat round out the premium materials of the RR. Harley made 131 of these bad boys. Some bought the bike as an investment. To sit as a garage queen until that time, when the secondary market prices make it unreasonable to keep. But others bought it as a gift to themselves. The ultimate performance bagger to commute, tour, and maybe even race on, if they're crazy enough. Luckily for those folks, Harley made sure that the RR's premium features bled into its electrical and digital guts as well. There are riding modes (for track riding and touring), advanced ABS brakes, and smart traction controls aplenty to make it as usable and as safe as possible. You'll also get the typical Harley bells and whistles in the form of its infotainment system. A 12.3-inch touchscreen houses Apple CarPlay, Bluetooth connectivity, and navigation. And to round out the package, you'll get the Rockford Fosgate State III audio system to let everyone know you're coming in hot. H-D has been building bikes since 1903. That's nothing. Level any accusation you want at the Bar and Shield builder. The one thing you can't say is that they don't know how to build a stone-cold classic. They've made tons of them over the years. Some of them continue to be sold even today, in one form or another. So too will the world come to remember the CVO Road Glide RR. Perhaps they'll hem and haw over its price and uber exclusivity. But we'd like to think that it will be remembered for its high level of pure craftsmanship instead. We want to hear from you. title: Title V/Clean Air Act: Sierra Club Petition to Object Filed Addressing Fairfield, Iowa Foundry - JD Supra
content:
The Iowa Chapter of the Sierra Club filed a Petition to Object (“Petition”) to the issuance of a Title V Operating Permit before the United States Environmental Protection Agency (“EPA”) addressing HyCast Foundry LLC (“HCF”). Sierra Club provides that HCF operates a grey and ductile foundry in Fairfield, Iowa. The Petition objects to the Iowa Department of Natural Resources’ (“IDNR”) renewal of the Title V Air Permit. Title V of the Clean Air Act requires certain stationary sources of air pollutants to obtain operating permits. The Clean Air Act provides that States administer Title V through adopted implementation plans. The intent of a Title V permit is to organize in a single document all the requirements that apply to the permit holder. 42 U.S.C. § 7661 requires that states submit each proposed Title V Permit to EPA for review. Section 505(b)(1) of the Clean Air Act requires that EPA object to the issuance of a proposed Title V Permit in writing within 45 days of the receipt of the proposed Permit (and all necessary supporting information) if the agency determines it is not in compliance with the applicable requirements of the Clean Air Act. If EPA does not object to a Permit, Section 505(b)(2) provides that any person may petition the EPA Administrator within 60 days of the expiration of the 45-day review period to object to the Permit. The HCF facility is described as manufacturing a variety of products, including: The facility is stated to use induction furnaces to melt scrap iron for production of ductile castings. Molten iron is then poured from the furnaces into ladles for magnesium inoculation (the production of ductile iron) and transported to the mold, pour, and cool lines. The castings continue through the production line to shakeout and various cleaning operations. The Petition argues that the Title V Permit renewal does not contain the required monitoring provisions in 40 C.F.R. § 70.6(3). It further states in part: … Even after the draft permit was issued despite objections made by Sierra Club members and others, HyCast failed a stack test on April 7, 2026. So the insufficient monitoring did not detect what turned out to be a violation of the particulate limits in the permit. The Petition further argues that although HCF has the potential to emit hazardous air pollutants (“HAPs”) over 25 tons per year, which is the threshold for stricter regulation, it claims to be a synthetic minor. This claim is stated to be premised on permit conditions that allegedly keep the actual emissions below 25 tpy. HCF’s application for a Title V Permit renewal is alleged to indicate that the actual potential to emit HAPs from the HyCast foundry is 40.53 tpy. The Petition alleges that the lack of adequate monitoring, analysis procedures, and test methods, means that there are no restrictions that are “enforceable as a practical matter” for the facility to be treated as a synthetic minor HAP source. Therefore, Sierra Club argues that the facility is not a minor source. Finally, the Petition alleges that the Compliance Assurance Monitoring plan is insufficient to demonstrate continuous compliance as a minor HAP source based on the previously referenced failed stack test. The facility is alleged to require more frequent stack test requirement and more frequent fugitive emissions testing involving EPA Method 9 of Opacity observations. title: Is It Better To Enable Or Disable V-Sync For Gaming? - BGR
content: Screen tearing is a phenomenon where weird artifacts appear on the screen during gameplay. It usually manifests as horizontal lines or looks as if multiple images are being shown at once. It's more noticeable when a lot of things are happening on screen, such as explosions and special effects. Another scenario is during fast movements, such as quick camera rotations. Vertical synchronization (V-sync) was created to solve the problem of screen tearing. A good rule of thumb is that if you don't notice screen tearing, keep V-sync off. Otherwise, enable it. Screen tearing happens when a high frame rate meets a low refresh rate. A frame rate is how many images the graphics processing unit (GPU) can render on screen per second, while a refresh rate is the number of times the monitor can update per second. So, with screen tearing, the graphics card would have sent several frames to the monitor before it had a chance to refresh its screen — for example, when a GPU pushes 60 FPS to a monitor with a refresh rate of 30 Hz. V-sync tells the GPU to wait for the screen to refresh before it renders a frame. If you have a monitor with the right refresh rate, it can keep up with your graphics card. If not, you can enable V-sync in the game's graphics settings. You can also enable it globally on your computer if your graphics card supports it. You just need to access its control panel and you should find the option in the graphics settings. V-sync can introduce another visual artifact — stuttering. For V-sync to work properly, it needs to match the frame rate to the refresh rate exactly. When the frame rate becomes lower than the refresh rate, that's another mismatch. If stuttering is not an issue, you might experience input lag. In most cases, the screen is holding the GPU back — but when V-sync makes the GPU wait, it can introduce input lag. Both stuttering and input lag can be a huge problem if you're a competitive player. You can miss shots and react slower, leading to frustrating losses. These issues can be ignored in most single-player games because you're playing alone and enemy AI is more predictable than humans. The same goes for much slower single-player games, such as turn-based RPGs like "Persona 5 Royal" and "Baldur's Gate 3." However, in games that require quick reflexes and timing, like "Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice" and "Hi-Fi Rush," it can lead to unnecessary deaths. If the input lag or stuttering is unbearable, it's best to see if your monitor supports FreeSync instead. It will essentially dynamically adjust your game's frame rate to match your monitor's refresh rate (as opposed to forcing it to wait). If there's no FreeSync and you have an Nvidia graphics card, you can turn on G-Sync instead. It does the same thing as FreeSync, but on the graphics card level. They're both types of adaptive sync technology, while V-sync is static.

title: Update: Kuilema v. Calvin at the Michigan Supreme Court - Calvin University Chimes
content: On Thursday, Oct. 8, the Michigan Supreme Court heard oral arguments in the landmark case Joseph Kuilema v. Calvin University. The case, which has worked through the Michigan courts for over three years, could set a new legal precedent for civil rights law in Michigan. The court’s decision, which has not been released, will determine whether Kuilema, a former Calvin University professor, can sue the university on a claim of sex-based associational discrimination under Michigan’s Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act (ELCRA). Kuilema was denied reappointment by Calvin in 2022 after he officiated a same-sex wedding and then sued the university on two claims: one based on sex-based associational discrimination and the second on retaliation. Under ELCRA, employers cannot discriminate against individuals’ employment based on sex, among other factors. The case before the court on Thursday focused on whether ELCRA provides standing for sex-based discrimination that is associational, where the claim is based on discrimination against a separate individual to the plaintiff. In Kuilema’s case, his associational claim is based on the couple whose wedding he officiated. Kuilema’s side, represented by counsel Charissa Huang, argued on Thursday that associational discrimination has already been established in cases of race and should therefore extend under ELCRA to sex-based claims. She said that “to recognize those claims but not these claims here … would go against the purpose of [ELCRA] to eliminate the effects of offensive and demeaning stereotypes, prejudices and biases.” Representing Calvin was Stephen J. van Stempvoort, who argued that discrimination under ELCRA can only be established on the basis of the plaintiff’s own sex, saying, “The plain text of the statute is actually pretty clear that it has to be the individual who is experiencing discrimination, that it has to be their protected characteristic that’s at issue.” Kuilema’s side argued in rebuttals that not allowing the associational claim for sex-based discrimination in this case would set the wrong precedent and “would have a chilling effect upon people of different races and cultures and sexes and sexual orientations [who] could be fired for associating with one another with no recourse. … That doesn’t align with the purpose of ELCRA.” The court’s ruling in this case does not have any bearing on Calvin’s argument based on religious freedom — that the university should be able to determine its hiring standards based on its theological beliefs. Kuilema spoke to the nuance of this specific part of the case, telling Chimes, “You can even imagine somebody who thinks that Calvin should be able to discriminate religiously, who supports the idea that associational discrimination on the basis of sex is a thing in Michigan.” The court may schedule further arguments at a later date, but if the decision by the Court of Appeals is not overturned by the Supreme Court, Kuilema will only be able to continue his lawsuit against Calvin under his claim of retaliation. The case has taken three years to make it to the Michigan Supreme Court and the civil trial is yet to begin in full. Still, Kuilema said that both he and Huang are “in it for the long haul.” Your email address will not be published. No Friend to Penumbras									 • 									Oct 12, 2026 at 9:19 am Justice Samuel Alito was right when he recently noted that creating the constitutional right to same-sex marriage dealt a staggering blow to religious liberty. But for the purposes of the litigation happening about this statute specifically, it seems to me that Kuilema’s representation is forcing their own vision of the good into a statute which, according to Calvin’s representation, says nothing of the sort. Upon reading this article, the ill-conceived attempt is very likely being tried for the sake of not setting “the wrong precedent.” It strikes me that judges ought not judge these things based on what one side *feels* is wrong. Rather, they ought to judge these things based on what the text of the statute says. This is called “textualism,” which is a theory largely developed and implemented by the late Justice Antonin Scalia. He has this to say: “Textualism means you are governed by the text. That is the only thing that is relevant to your decision, not whether the outcome is desirable, not whether legislative history says this or that. But the text of the statute.” Should the MI high court side with Kuilema, reading their own vision of the common good into a statute where that isn’t even remotely present, I will look forward to SCOTUS slapping them on the wrist with an honest, textualist ruling — based on the rich precedent set by Scalia and his peers. And hopefully, as the Roberts Court has been known to do, they will protect religious liberty while they’re at it.

Green Oceans, a Rhode Island-based environmental organization, announced the discovery of what it believes is the F/V Mistress in the waters off Block Island in September. Michael Lombardi, president of Green Oceans, told Fox News Digital his organization began searching for the vessel after receiving tips from two contractors who had previously worked near turbine No. 1 at the Block Island Wind Farm. One contractor reported hearing rumors of underwater wreckage — while another claimed to have personally spotted wreckage while conducting survey work at the site. YOUNG NEWLYWEDS KILLED AFTER BOAT COLLIDES WITH WATER TAXI AND SINKS IN VENICE LAGOON Lombardi said he later reviewed the Coast Guard's original accident report and plotted GPS coordinates associated with distress calls and other key details, which pointed investigators toward the turbine. Lombardi said he hopes federal authorities will reopen the investigation to determine whether the two fishermen who died remain within the wreckage or were swept out to sea and whether such a maneuver contributed to the sinking. title: Coventry v Newcastle: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Coventry celebrated their first Premier League goal and points for more than 25 years by beating Nottingham Forest before the international break. Monday night's visitors Newcastle have won all seven league and cup meetings this century between the two, albeit the clubs haven't faced each other since February 2010. The caveat to Coventry's run of four straight league defeats from the start of the season was that it included away games against last season's top two sides. In a more favourable-looking run this month, they have three home fixtures out of four and will face the two teams who sat below them going into the latest round of matches. Having felled Forest, Coventry are attempting to become the first English side in 127 years to earn consecutive top-flight wins immediately after losing their opening four games without scoring. Derby County are the only club to do so, in 1899, and they rallied to finish sixth. A far more modern precedent to give Coventry some belief is that three promoted sides have started as badly as them in the Premier League and still avoided relegation. Head coach Frank Lampard hopes his team can take inspiration from the memory of their most recent Monday night home game, an outstanding 3-1 win over Middlesbrough in February. Coventry were second to Boro going into that fixture after losing a 10-point lead, but victory put them back on top and they pulled away to clinch the Championship title. "I watch parts of that game back regularly because it was our outstanding game last year considering what was on it," said Lampard. "And now we have to do 38 (sic) versions of that kind of feeling to get things nailed on." Newcastle are playing promoted opponents for the second match in a row, having held off a late fightback to end Hull City's unbeaten start to the season. That result, coupled with a high-tempo first-half display, made partial amends for the dismal 4-1 defeat at Leeds United five days earlier. Newcastle's defensive vulnerability is clear; they faced a league-high 97 shots across their opening five games. Nonetheless, a tally of eight points from five games is a solid start under Matthias Jaissle – especially in the wake of a tumultuous summer during which they sold their three highest-profile players. Despite injuries hindering Newcastle's youthful rebuild, a win on Monday would give Jaissle the joint-second best start by a Magpies manager after six Premier League games.

Broadcaster and journalist Nick Peet, British heavyweight champion Richard Riakporhe, and BBC Sounds' Punch Perfect hosts Emily Smith and Liam Gough will provide live reaction, analysis, debate and discussion as the fight unfolds. The official time for the event is yet to be confirmed, but Dubois and Wardley are expected to make their ringwalks after 22:30 BST. Daniel Dubois v Fabio Wardley - WBO heavyweight title Louie O'Doherty v Michael Gomez Jr - British and Commonwealth lightweight title Leighton Birchall v Luis Vara Carrillo - featherweight Issiah Hamilton-Allen v Jensen Irving - middleweight There is very little between Dubois and Wardley physically, and almost nothing between them when it comes to punching power. Dubois knows he can beat Wardley and Wardley knows he can hurt Dubois. Dubois has 23 wins from 26 fights, with 22 knockouts, while Wardley's record stands at 20 wins, one defeat and one draw, with 19 knockouts. That means 41 of their combined 43 victories have come inside the distance. Where Dubois holds the advantage is experience at the highest level. He has twice fought Oleksandr Usyk and has also shared the ring with Anthony Joshua, Filip Hrgovic and Joe Joyce. Wardley's route has been far less conventional. He came through the unlicensed white-collar scene and was working in recruitment at the age of 19. But his rise accelerated with stoppage wins over Justis Huni and former world champion Joseph Parker before his first meeting with Dubois. Dubois' WBO world heavyweight title is at stake over 12 three-minute rounds. It will be the first defence of his second reign as a world champion. Dubois previously held the IBF heavyweight title before losing his rematch with Usyk in July 2025. Wardley became WBO champion after being elevated from interim champion but lost the belt to Dubois in his first defence. The WBO belt is now one of four major heavyweight titles, which are held by four different fighters. Dubois holds the WBO belt, Agit Kabayel is WBC champion, Filip Hrgovic has the IBF title and Murat Gassiev is recognised by the WBA as its world champion. The first fight at Manchester's Co-op Live Arena had almost everything - knockdowns, momentum shifts, heavy exchanges and a remarkable comeback. Wardley made a sensational start, twice dropping Dubois, but the fight swung as Dubois recovered and eventually forced an 11th-round stoppage. But it became increasingly uncomfortable to watch. Wardley fought on despite a badly damaged nose and one eye being swollen shut, with doctors checking him twice at ringside before allowing the contest to continue. By the 10th round he was struggling badly and there were calls for the fight to have been stopped earlier. Former world champion Carl Frampton described Wardley as the "bravest man he'd ever seen", but said the referee or his corner should have intervened before the 10th, while Darren Barker called for the fight to be stopped to protect Wardley. The statistics underline the punishment he absorbed. Dubois landed 179 punches to Wardley's 97, with 87 power punches by Dubois compared with Wardley's 40. But both men emerged with reputations enhanced. Wardley's willingness to keep fighting demonstrated extraordinary heart, while Dubois answered questions which had followed him earlier in his career about his own resilience. The heavyweight landscape could look very different by the end of the year. Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will finally meet at Cardiff's Principality Stadium in December, more than a decade after a fight between the British rivals was first discussed. Their bout has reportedly been earmarked for a WBA 'super' heavyweight title, although that has proved controversial. Gassiev remains listed by the WBA as its world champion and his team have lodged an objection to the prospect of another WBA heavyweight champion being crowned. But it means the winner of Dubois-Wardley could enter 2027 with several lucrative options. For Dubois, another victory would settle his rivalry with Wardley at 2-0 and give him a successful first defence of his second world title reign. At the age of 29, wins over Joshua, Hrgovic and Wardley twice would leave Dubois with one of the strongest recent records among the division's leading heavyweights. Unification fights against Kabayel or Hrgovic would be obvious targets, while the winner of Fury-Joshua could provide another huge all-British option depending on how the WBA title situation develops. For Wardley, victory would see him regain the title, avenge the only defeat of his career and put himself firmly in the conversation for unification fights. The consequences of defeat are slightly different, though. A second successive loss to Dubois would leave Wardley needing to rebuild before another world title opportunity. Should Dubois lose, the rivalry would stand at 1-1 and calls for a third fight would begin almost immediately. (NYSE:V) operates a global payments network, earning fees from payment volumes, transaction processing, and related services. Banks issue cards and extend credit; the company connects financial institutions and merchants without funding consumers' card balances. Digital commerce and international spending expand that opportunity, but banks and merchants want a share of the growth. The company appears in Insider Monkey's 10 Most Profitable Blue Chip Stocks to Buy According to Hedge Funds. The investment question is whether its network retains enough profit after client rebates to justify the earnings multiple. Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) benefits when wider acceptance makes its network more useful to cardholders, attracting additional banks and merchants. Reliability, fraud controls and established integrations reinforce that advantage. New payment channels create value when they expand profitable activity, the same distinction as when a new checkout channel adds payment revenue. Fiscal Q3 2026 processed transactions increased 10%, while cross-border volume excluding transactions within Europe grew 12% in constant dollars. Value-added services generated $3.8 billion of revenue. Security, acceptance and advisory tools can deepen relationships and improve revenue per customer. Maintaining that advantage requires technology, personnel and marketing spending. Competing networks and direct bank-payment options can strengthen clients' bargaining power. Incentives create value when the additional revenue they secure covers both concessions and associated operating costs, leaving an adequate profit. Network scale supports a premium only when those relationships produce profitable repeat business. Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) carries approximately 26x forward P/E and 33x trailing P/E. Trailing P/E uses historical reported earnings; forward P/E uses forecast earnings. The forward valuation looks fair given sustained transaction growth and strong profitability, provided client concessions and operating costs leave enough room for earnings to compound. Analysts expect adjusted EPS of approximately $15.00 in fiscal 2027, ending September, versus $13.23 for fiscal 2026, implying 13% growth. Expected revenue growth of approximately 11% supplies much of the operating foundation. Additional services, pricing, and share repurchases can help EPS grow faster than sales. Reported earnings and adjusted forecasts also use different accounting treatments. Q3 reported EPS was $2.97, versus non-GAAP adjusted EPS of $3.32. Severance and certain litigation provisions explain most of that gap. The $563 million severance charge depressed reported earnings, while management plans to reinvest workforce savings in growth opportunities. Its disappearance could improve a future GAAP comparison. Because adjusted earnings already exclude that charge, forecast growth in adjusted EPS must come from improvements elsewhere. Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) reported 17% growth in non-GAAP operating expenses in Q3, exceeding 14% net-revenue growth. Some personnel-expense growth reflected deferred-compensation remeasurement offset by investment income, so that component did not reduce EPS. Marketing, technology, and employee spending still require productive returns, illustrating why faster payments do not automatically produce wider margins. Buybacks also contributed: adjusted net income increased 8%, while adjusted EPS rose 11%. Reducing the share count can support per-share growth, but requires cash that also funds client contracts and reinvestment. The current 26x forward P/E for Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) compares with approximately 26x on September 19, 2024, and 27x at its September 2025 fiscal year-end. Investors are paying roughly the same multiple as in the earlier observation and modestly less than at the later year-end. That offers little evidence of a substantial historical bargain. Adjusted EPS grew 15% in fiscal 2024 and 14% in 2025. The 13% growth forecast for 2027 supports a broadly similar valuation, while stronger cash conversion would be needed to make a higher multiple compelling. The operating demands behind today's valuation deserve attention. Client incentives increased 14% against 17% net-revenue growth in fiscal Q2 2026. In Q3, those rates became 18% and 14%. Management attributed faster incentive growth partly to unusually low growth in the prior-year comparison and stronger client performance. It expected Q4 incentive growth slightly above Q3 as renewals and new business added costs. Incentives are already deducted from net revenue. Measured against revenue before those deductions, they absorbed approximately 28.7% in Q3, versus 28.1% a year earlier. About one-third of incremental revenue before incentives went into additional concessions. Across nine months, however, the proportion remained approximately 28.1%, versus 28.2%. The longer period supports the existing valuation, while the quarterly deterioration helps explain why a return to a higher multiple needs stronger evidence. The test remains how much loyalty is worth after customers receive their rewards. Cash generation adds another requirement for Visa Inc. (NYSE:V). Subtracting $1.18 billion of capital expenditure from nine-month operating cash flow of $16.34 billion leaves approximately $15.16 billion, down from $15.73 billion. Higher litigation and incentive payments, alongside tax-payment timing, contributed to the decline. Upfront incentives can consume cash before being recognized against revenue, so contract growth must eventually replenish the cash committed to winning it. Mastercard Incorporated (NYSE:MA) is the closest operating peer because both companies earn network fees and sell related services without directly financing cardholder balances. Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) and Mastercard Incorporated (NYSE:MA) both carry approximately 26x forward P/E. For the same calendar quarter ending December 2026, analysts expect adjusted EPS growth of approximately 14% and 9%, respectively. That is fiscal Q1 2027 for the primary company and Q4 2026 for the peer. Faster expected near-term growth supports the similar multiples, although ongoing profitability matters beyond that quarter. For the June quarter, the primary company's calculated adjusted operating margin was 66.7%, down from 67.5%. The peer's adjusted margin rose to 61.1% from 59.9%, as 14% revenue growth outpaced 11% adjusted expense growth. The primary company retains the higher adjusted margin; the peer shows the stronger recent margin trend. Customer bargaining power affects both networks. The peer's payment-network rebates and incentives rose 22%, reflecting transaction growth and new or renewed contracts. Its improving margin shows that larger concessions can coexist with profitable expansion when services and operating efficiency compensate. Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) also had approximately $11.5 billion of borrowings less cash and cash equivalents in June, versus $13.4 billion for the peer. Its larger quarterly operating-profit base and lower net debt provide more financial room. title: Liverpool v Man City player ratings: Florian Wirtz has tough game for Reds - BBC
content: Highlights: Manchester City beat Liverpool to extend perfect start Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scored as Manchester City inflicted a first defeat for Liverpool on Andoni Iraola. Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below. Premier League: Man City cruise to statement win at 10-man Liverpool - reaction Alisson: Could do nothing to keep out Erling Haaland's strike then beaten by a beauty from Jeremy Doku and some solid footwork from Rayan Cherki. 5 Ronald Araujo: Got a cheap yellow card early on and will be annoyed that the first two Man City goals came from his side. 5 Virgil van Dijk: Often pushed out of position to help Liverpool deal with getting outnumbered in midfield. Perhaps could have closed Haaland down quicker. 6 Jeremy Jacquet: Wasn't a bad display from a young talent who is very impressive but this must have been a real eye-opener against a quality City attack. 6 Milos Kerkez: Battled well with Iliman Ndiaye and pushed up regularly but lacked  quality in the final third. 5 Alexis Mac Allister: Grew into the game and put in a good shift but struggled once Liverpool went down to 10 men. 5 Ryan Gravenberch: Came in for the injured Dominik Szoboszlai and was Liverpool's best player until he got sent off for a second yellow card. Naive on his part. 6 Victor Munoz: Played with such a fearlessness and was an absolute nuisance for Man City, causing Nico O'Reilly all sorts of problems. 7 Florian Wirtz: Simply has to do better, particularly in games of this magnitude. Was largely ineffective and made some poor decisions. 4 Bradley Barcola: Sharp on the ball and did his defensive duties but, like Wirtz, must to do more in the final third. 5 Lewis Koumas: Making his first Premier League start and the 21-year-old got stuck in from the outset in an energetic display that was loved by the Anfield crowd. 7 Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, McConnell, Gianluigi Donnarumma: Had a shaky start but made a string of good saves early in the second half to deny Koumas and Gravenberch and keep the game level. 7 Matheus Nunes: An impressive display and made a great tackle in the box to deny Barcola in the first half. 7 Ruben Dias: Did well to weather the early storm and keep Liverpool out. 7 Marc Guehi: Like Dias, a strong performance at centre-half and can take satisfaction from the way they defended, especially when Liverpool attacked The Kop end. 7 Nico O'Reilly: Solid going forward but had his work cut out against Munoz and was inevitably booked when he fouled the Spaniard in the second-half. 6 Elliot Anderson: Always showed for the ball and constantly involved but lucky not to get booked for pulling Gravenberch back. Got the assist for Doku. 7 Enzo Fernandez: Forced Alisson to make a good stop in the first half but didn't really grow into the game until Gravenberch was sent off. 6 Iliman Ndiaye: Dangerous on the ball and had a few threatening moments before he was replaced by Doku. 6 Rayan Cherki: Capped off a day to remember for Man City with a lovely goal. 8 Antoine Semenyo: Threatening all afternoon and part of an attack that was simply too good for Liverpool once City had the man advantage. 7 Erling Haaland: Had a quiet first half and missed a huge chance early on in the second half but finished emphatically to give City the lead. 8 Doku (on 56, Ndiaye): Came on and scored an absolute belter. 8 Subs not used: Rulli, Kovacic, Reis, Khusanov, Lewis After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users. title: NFL today: How to watch 49ers v Seahawks, TV channels & live stream Sunday 11 October - The Guardian
content: How will the Seahawks and 49ers fare today? Here is what to know, including kick-off time, TV channels and live stream options Last winter, two games between the 49ers and Seahawks decided the shape of the NFL season. The two teams played each other in the Bay Area on the last weekend of the regular season, and Seattle’s win secured the NFC West and homefield advantage when the teams met later in the NFC divisional playoffs. Seattle’s advantage only got more lopsided at home, and a 41-6 win proved to be the launching pad that sent the Seahawks flying through the rest of the playoffs, ending with a Super Bowl victory. The Niners watched from home. Now they meet again in one of the most anticipated games of the 2026 season to date. The 49ers take an unbeaten record on the road against a 3-1 Seattle team who have kept the train on the tracks despite Sam Darnold getting hurt early in Week 1 and missing a game. Whoever wins here will claim divisional favorite status as we move into the second quarter of the season, and they’ll also give themselves a good shot to claim a head-to-head tiebreaker that may be important in the league’s most competitive division. United States: Watch on Fox or stream on Fox One or Fubo (where the local Fox affiliate carries the game). United Kingdom: Watch on Sky Sports NFL or stream on NOW The main man to watch for Seattle is the same as ever: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who just had one of the handful of most productive receiving seasons ever and is so far averaging more yards per game (120) than he did when he won Offensive Player of the Year. The Seahawks do not have a clear No 2 wideout and have some running back problems, too, given that Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker now plays for the Chiefs and first-round rookie Jadarian Price went to injured reserve this week. But as long as an offense has JSN, it has a chance to put up serious point totals. The Seahawks’ 105 points in four games are tied for sixth in the NFC. They’ll rise up the ranks if non-JSN contributors emerge. The 49ers are a more balanced juggernaut at the moment. Brock Purdy continues to be Brock Purdy, putting up terrific numbers in a maximally supportive system. A large handful of offensive players on the wrong side of 30 have all maintained their access to the fountain of youth: Trent Williams blocking, Christian McCaffrey running and catching, and Mike Evans, George Kittle, and Deebo Samuel as downfield targets. An injured defensive front (currently missing star edge rusher Nick Bosa and tackle James Thompson) has not stopped the 49ers’ defense from giving up the third-fewest yards per play in the NFL. The only trouble is that the two teams ahead of them are the Seahawks and Rams. Will this division put three teams in the playoff again? It looks that way.
